Industry Examples: law firm, legal, finance, private bank, luxury, institution
Pairing Filter: serif heading + serif or neutral-sans body (old-style or transitional serif; Didone for luxury)
Rationale: Serifs signal tradition, trust and institutional permanence — the dominant convention in legal and financial identity.
Evidence Gap: Serif convention is Western-print-rooted; verify legibility and tone for non-Latin scripts.

Industry Examples: research, education, journalism, consultancy, think tank
Pairing Filter: serif heading + humanist-sans body, or an all-serif editorial pairing
Body Class: humanist sans or a readable serif
Rationale: Editorial serif pairings read as authoritative and support sustained reading.
Evidence Gap: Screen-first products may prefer a high-legibility sans body over a serif.

Rationale: Geometric sans reads as forward-looking and clean, matching a transformation promise.
Evidence Gap: Geometric sans is over-used in tech; differentiate via weight, tracking and a distinctive display cut.

Pairing Filter: condensed grotesque heading + neutral-sans body, italic display accent
Rationale: Condensed weights compress energy and read as athletic and decisive.
Evidence Gap: Condensed faces lose legibility at small sizes and tight measures.

Rationale: Humanist sans feels friendly and unpretentious — the right register for mass appeal.
Evidence Gap: Risk of generic default-sans sameness; add a small distinctive detail.

Pairing Filter: soft humanist-sans heading + humanist-sans body, rounded optional
Rationale: Soft humanist forms read as warm and safe without losing professionalism.
Evidence Gap: Rounded faces can read juvenile in clinical or regulated contexts.

Pairing Filter: heavy grotesque or brutalist display heading + neutral-sans body
Rationale: High-impact display signals rule-breaking and stands out against polished incumbents.
Evidence Gap: Display-heavy systems fail accessibility at body sizes; constrain to headlines.

Pairing Filter: high-contrast serif (Didone) heading + humanist-sans body, optional script accent
Rationale: High-contrast serifs read as refined and desirable, central to beauty and fashion identity.
Evidence Gap: Didone hairlines vanish below ~24px and on low-DPI screens — set a minimum heading size.

Pairing Filter: rounded or quirky display heading + rounded-sans body
Rationale: Rounded and quirky faces carry warmth and play, matching a fun-first promise.
Evidence Gap: Novelty display faces date quickly and can undercut trust.

Pairing Filter: distinctive display heading + clean grotesque body
Rationale: A distinctive display face signals craft and originality; a neutral workhorse keeps it usable.
Evidence Gap: Distinctive display risks legibility — always pair with a neutral body workhorse.

Pairing Filter: condensed or slab heading + humanist-sans body
Rationale: Slab and condensed weights read as sturdy and outdoorsy.
Evidence Gap: Slab at body size feels heavy; reserve it for headings.
